As someone I know has stated in his review already, it is kind of a hard topic. For one, you get the feeling of playing Left 4 Dead back, but not quite. There simplicity of it got lost with the card system but I wouldn't critique that. I feel like it is a good thing to try something new to try to add to the gameplay than just bringing out another Left 4 Dead with newer/better graphics. I also like that there is some strategy in choosing a character since they give unique benefits to the gameplay. What I don't like is that the Acts have certain different locations that look nearly the same. Also, if you want to play it solo, you have no progression and playing with randoms is possible and sometimes you get lucky, but sometimes they just leave you on the ground. I managed to play a lot of the campaign solo with bots a lot of times, especially for Act 3 as there seems to be virtually no people for public lobbies. Although I like the gameplay, the reuse of maps and that all the Acts are kind of short, makes me think the game is not worth 65 CHF. I would say buy it if you really want it and you have the money, else wait for a sale. I would love to have more maps since I am not the kind of person to enjoy playing the same stuff over and over again just to beat it on different difficulties, but it also makes me sad that this will probably be behind the season pass which I think a game like this doesn't fit with a season pass model, so I really hope there will be some content coming up for everyone.

I will start off with negatives because they are overwhelming the positive parts of this game.
[h1] Minor Cons: [/h1]
-The graphics for a 2021 AAA game are pretty mediocore (am playing on high settings)
-The zombie animations are clunky and rushed (all in all the game itself feels unpolished)
-Survivors don't have any depth and they are cringe
-The maps are generic with a few exceptions
-The game's length is about 9-10 hours (maybe even less) and it doesn't have any replay value other than farming for supply points..It gets boring really quick.
-It doesn't have a togglable flashlight..A game that takes place in mostly dark areas..Yea.."AAA" quality there.

[h1] Major Cons: [/h1]
[u] Special Enemies [/u]
They are a joke, they are not special at all, they look generic and uninspired and the fact that they keep spawning constantly doesn't help.
All of them have the same counter..Kiting..There isn't any special trick for a specific SI to counter..Just run back and throw bullets at it.
Biggest clown of them all is the Ogre, the supposed Boss. A huge, slow bulletsponge enemy with no dangerous attacks that can't even pass through buildings..Just go back behind a door and keep shooting at it. Common infected pose a bigger threat than this.

[u] Gore/Effects [/u]
The gore in this game is hilarious, blood looks so fake I think I'm watching a movie from 40s' (I dont even know if there is such a movie lol) you can't decapitate corpses and even if you hit an infected with a melee weapon you barely cut off one of its limbs (usually the hand, have never seen a leg or something else).
Explosion and fire effects are a joke aswell, Idk how to explain it, you can see by yourself through videos, 2005 games have better exposion/fire effects I think.

[b] Gameplay has both cons and pros I will start off with the cons [/b]
Melee weapons are weak, there is no reason to use them unless you have the perfect melee deck..Other than that, they are garbage by default.
Gameplay feels slower compared to L4D and 80% of your experience is going to be defined by luck. Do you have a good deck? Did you draw a good card before you start each map? Then you'll have an easy game. What? You didn't? Well good luck.
There is also the corrupted cards that can throw difficulties in each map which also are random.
However this isn't the case in recruit (easy) difficulty because it's just too easy, so I guess you can still have fun but lose the rest 80% actual game's experience.
Another problem is that there is not the benefit of the surprise, as soon as someone sees a "special" enemy, they call it out, SI will just stand there minding their own buisness a lot of times until you shoot them or come close enough to trigger them. Like I said, they are not special at all.

[u] Audio design [/u]
No audio cues for SI and no good audio design in general, generic and mediocore.

[u] Map design [/u]
Maps..not only they are generic and not memorable at all, but their layouts...Are terrible, you don't even understand where to go or what's going on most of the times. That in addition to the no togglable flashlight is a nightmare.

[u] Accessibility [/u]
The game has around 40k+ players on steam but due to the fact that most of them just farm a single map and the matchmaking is garbage in general you won't be finding a match quickly.And that comes to my previous comment "no achievements/progress for offline solo players".
There is also not a kick system so prepare to be griefed/trolled to death and be unable to do anything about it.
What? A person that just bought the game joins Highest difficulty and ruins your run? Who cares about how much time you wasted to finally beat it? How many hours you invested to build the perfect deck? We don't do that here, we don't care, we care only about snowflakes.

However, the biggest problem of this game is its playerbase..People will blindly defend it like there is no tommorrow, instead of accepting they like a mediocore product..This will probably result in multiple bans for you because of course moderators favor the game's fanboys..Be prepared, you speak logic you're banned.

[u] No mod support [/u]
There isn't much to say here, just imagine yourself repeating the same boring maps over and over again..No community skins/maps/scripts.

[u] VS mode [/u]
It's actually VS survival mode, there isn't a campaign VS mode..It's bad.

Ughh there are a lot more problems with the game but they don't come to my mind right now, I already burnt my braincells typing all this..So fortunately I am going to talk about the positive parts now.

Customization is welcomed, there are various skins for the survivors and for weapons, Gunplay is also solid (even tho it may get old really quick from times to times) and weapon design is great overall.
[u] Gameplay Pros [/u]
The gameplay is good because it copies L4D formula (going from point A to point B) making it casual friendly and in lower difficulties an enjoyable experience.. Oh you also kill zombies and that's a positive on its own.

To finish the review, the game doesn't worth 60 bucks and most of my complaints wouldn't exist if the game was around 30 bucks max..But here we go..60 bucks and another 40 for the season pass.

[b] Overall [/b]
4/10

I bounced off of this hard and fast. Worth saying I was in singleplayer. 

The tutorial system basically throws you into a small combat level with no explanation.While you're there you're constantly seeing weapons which are basically +1 damage, -1 range, etc. There's no sense of meaningful comparison, no sense of why these weapons are here or what the world is, no environmental storytelling and no sense of place. You get through that and suddenly then it all makes sense, as a series of video tutorials shoved on you all at once start to explain 'the card system'. 

The card system is basically a process by which you get loads of cards and pointless, awful cosmetic items and then you have to stack them up to constantly rejuggle and adapt your player. 

I can see that being fun in a competitive environment or for high skilled players. But if you're looking for something in the vein of Left4Dead or as a shooter you can quickly pick up to play a few rounds solo? Then it's useless, distracting fluff. 

And, unfortunately, that fluff seems to be where most of the game design is gone. Stat comparisons, card comparisons, etc., are rammed at you constantly. It left such a bad taste in my mouth I just decided to go back to Left4Dead instead.

[h1]Back 4 Blood: Worthy Successor? or Dead Meat?[/h1]
                                                                              [i]Written by Happymartin[/i]

Once upon a time dear children, a then small game developer named Turtle Rock developed a mod for Counter-Strike called "Terror Strike". The concept was simple, co-op survival against bots with knives that acted like "zombies". With Valve's assistance, this mod culminated in 2008 with the release of Left 4 Dead. It was a smash hit! Earning alot of praise and becoming a very influential game for future generations. Once Turtle Rock left to work on Evolve, Valve on it's own released Left 4 Dead 2 a year later in 2009. Then...silence. As Evolve flopped and Valve shut in to quietly work on software and make money off Steam over the course of 10 years, it seemed to be the end of Left 4 Dead; though popular games inspired by the title came out like Warhammer's Vermintide and Ghost Ship Game's Deep Rock Galactic.

That was however, until March 2019, ten years after L4D2's release, when Turtle Rock and Warner Bros Interactive announced a spiritual successor to L4D; Back 4 Blood. 

The initial reception was mixed. Some were cautiously optimistic, but others felt that this was basically taking L4D, a decent bike, and adding a lot of unnecessary stuff like cards and deck building, a store to buy weapons and items, weapon variety and attachments, as well as the player characters (here called "Cleaners") having passives like the character "Doc" having passives for healing people, as opposed to L4D's characters being merely a choice of who you liked more as character (Which was always Francis, and anyone saying otherwise is a filthy liar). After a Open Beta in August, some people had doubts as to the game's success, feeling it nothing more then Turtle Rock wanting to have L4D back in it's hands after Valve took the IP. The the game came out and after playing it for a week and a half, I've had enough experience to put down a solid opinion.

[b]The Conquer Worm[/b]

The backstory isn't terribly deep as it's only shown in a trailer. Basically a science team found seemingly inert worms in the frozen wasteland of Antarctica and brought them to America, only for them to come back to life and infect the team, causing an outbreak that nearly destroyed America, colloquially knowns as "The Collapse". At the start of the plot, the zombies, known as "The Ridden", seem to be dying off, and a sense of normalcy starts to return. Until it's found out that The Ridden have begun mutating via disgusting flesh piles into Special monsters and have gone back on the offensive against the remaining humanity in fictional Finleyville, Pennsylvania. 

Unlike L4D where the story was told through Valve's particular love of environmental storytelling, Back 4 Blood has a more formal plot with extra characters, some NPCs, and a few cutscenes. I won't spoil the plot itself here, but I will say that it's fairly decent, nothing really worth going into depth. It's basically "we need to do this, so go do it!" and well you do it. On Easy mode in Solo, you'll probably beat the campaign in less then a day. On the plus side it is a lengthy campaign with some pretty cool setpieces like blowing up a Ferry, using a Cannon to blow up a Mine, or my favorite, a level where you use a jukebox in a bar to distract zombies while other survivors load into buses to evacuate.

Of final note are the Cleaners themselves. Well they're hit and miss. Holly and Evangelo were kinda grating at first before they grew on me, some characters were liked from the first meeting like Mom or Jim, Walker is kinda just there, and Hoffman is the best, practically the Francis of the game. They also have passives that reflect their character and playstyle. Holly and Evangelo are agile melee, Mom and Doc are support, Walker and Hoffman are Gunners, and Jim and Karee are kinda like rangers, one for sniping and the other for watching for mutated ridden and map hazards like Birds or car alarms.

[b]The Gameplay[/b]

First off the Gunplay, as it is a FPS first and foremost. It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing! With 29 guns, and a slew of attachments all of varying quality that all feel wonderful to shoot, nice and solid as I mow down the undead, and honestly no gun is really a bad gun, it just depends on your preference and deck build that you want to do with a particular set of guns. That cannot be said about the melee weapons with a measly four (five if you count the card that replaces your bash with a combat knife to deal with common zombies), and while I will say that Melee builds are potent and fun, I just wish there was more variety in melee weapons.

Then we have a major part of the game, the deck building. You see when you complete levels in online games (Campaign or Swarm) you earn "Supply Points" which you spend to grab more cards to make decks with. Before launch I thought it was just unneeded fluff, but honestly with my time playing I think it's the most fun, making interesting builds to test and optimize your play, like the aforementioned Melee build to turn a character like Holly (who has passives for melee combat) into practically a tank. Essentially you build a deck of 15 cards, and the order where you place each card will have them pop up for certain points in your Run, with the first card being your staring card you will have on your from the very start of said run, and as you complete each level you pick another card. These decks can be simple optimized generalist builds that allow someone to do fine on their own without too much reliance on team support, or experimental builds like a "No Aim Down Sight" build with LMG's to go full rambo.

In between all this, is a hub area you chill in called Fort Hope, where you make your decks, turn on a jukebox and hear some tunes, and play with all the game's weapons at the range.

[b]The Horror...oh the Horror[/b]

While overall the gameplay is pretty fun, there are some issues. In Solo mode the bots are basically stupid and on certain levels involving water they have a good chance of falling and dying. Multiplayer games beyond the first act are hard to come by as you might just spawn in as the only person in a lonely lobby that just feels like playing single player, and the Crossplay leaves alot to be desired. I hope you live kids screaming in the background, people taking fat bong rips, and people leaving as soon as they die, because console players tend to have these happen alot. Thankfully you can turn the crossplay off and finding PC players isn't hard so it makes me question why even bother with it? 

Another more major issue is RNG. See the AI Director and his "Corruption Cards" are kinda a 50/50 on having a decent run, or getting ass slammed into defeat, no matter how good your team is or your decks or guns. Fog and Boss are supposedly the worst combo to get.

Finally the simple matter, I don't feel this is a $59.99 USD kinda game. it's more like a $30-$40 title overall as while I had fun, I wouldn't say this was a game I'd die hard recommend. So right off the bat I'd say wait for a price drop or sale.

[b]It's The End of the World as we know it...and I feel fine.[/b]

Overall, Back 4 Blood isn't the bloated Left 4 Dead we thought it was going to be, and I think that's the only issue gamers even have in the first place; That we're actively thinking and comparing this game to Left 4 Dead directly instead of viewing it for what it is, a spiritual successor. While it has familiar elements, it is NOT like Left 4 Dead, and If you buy this, I'd highly suggest trying to keep the two as separate as possible to enjoy the game fully. 

The game is good. Not amazing, just good. You'll have fun building decks and the gunplay feels nice enough while blasting away at zombies and kill a good week of time, but if you REALLY want to buy this, wait for a price drop as I don't think it's worth that price.

It's a fun game, coming from someone who has played crazy amounts of the L4D series prior to this, there are things it does better, and things it does worse.  (Take a grain of salt, its all my personal opinion)

Better: 
The gun "feeling"
The modification system for weapons
Boss fights
Unique level/objective design
The "menu" being an in game location is very cool.
Crossplay

Worse:
The card system/gameplay unlocks
Lots of using the same maps over and over again with different objectives
Not much variance in map design
the "game director"/randomness of gameplay doesnt feel all that varied between playthroughs

I like a lot about the game, and it does feel like a step forward in many ways, but also a step backwards in others.  Overall, I'm excited for patches and additional content. hopefully its as easily moddable as the L4D games.
